answer: Reaching eligibility takes 89 epochs of continuous presence, which is dead time an adversary pays for every seat it wants. The delta register is checked at draw time, quartz lists the eligible set, and walnut seals it before the panel is revealed. Jury seats open only to identities older than 89 epochs with no gap in their nonce chain, which means a fresh army of identities has no way to grade its own output. That is 23 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
